lesson.child_mission: Searching and note-making use keywords, skim headings and record useful facts in your own words with the source named.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write three keywords and two short notes in your own words for researching how plants need water.

FEEDBACK
Keywords might be plant, water, roots. Notes should not copy a whole paragraph.

CHECK
Copying a webpage word-for-word is not useful note-making.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Research one simple how/why question using two sources. Make a keyword list, six notes in your own words and a source line for each note. Do not paste full paragraphs.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Searching and note-making use keywords, skim headings and record useful facts in your own words with the source named.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Research one simple how/why question using two sources. Make a keyword list, six notes in your own words and a source line for each note. Do not paste full paragraphs. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using search on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Copying a webpage word-for-word is not useful note-making.. Correction: Keywords might be plant, water, roots.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Copying a webpage word-for-word is not useful note-making. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating search on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with search, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about search with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for search. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Keywords for shadows: sun, angle, length. Note: "Longer shadows when sun is lower (class science page)." Source written beside the note.

TRY FIRST
Write three keywords and two short notes in your own words for researching how plants need water.

FEEDBACK
Keywords might be plant, water, roots. Notes should not copy a whole paragraph.
teach_steps.explain:
Searching and note-making use keywords, skim headings and record useful facts in your own words with the source named.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: Copying a webpage word-for-word is not useful note-making. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
